definition: A spliceosomopathy is a genetic disease caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding components or regulators of the pre-mRNA splicing machinery, such as splicing factors like TRA2B (Tra2β). Disruption of these proteins compromises cellular splicing patterns, leading to aberrant transcript processing and manifesting as developmental delay, intellectual disability, and other neurological phenotypes.

source.quote: Transformer2 proteins (Tra2α and Tra2β) control splicing patterns in human cells, and no human phenotypes have been associated with germline variants in these genes.
